repo_notes.content: moqtail/moqtail is a Rust and TypeScript MOQT monorepo with root Cargo and npm workspaces. Rust crates and applications live under rs/ (moqtail, moqtail-ssts, client, relay); TypeScript packages and applications live under ts/ (moqtail, client-js, meet). Other top-level directories include dev/conformance/draft22/ for Draft 22 conformance data and scripts/ for project automation. Shared configuration and automation include .changeset, .github, and .husky. Relay certificates are under rs/relay/cert. The relay server is published as a Docker image to ghcr.io/moqtail/relay. License is Apache-2.0. Citation/academic reference: Gurel, Ugur, Begen, 'MOQtail: open-source, IETF-compliant MOQT protocol libraries,' ACM MMSys 2026.

Two protocol implementations exist side by side: the Rust moqtail crate at rs/moqtail/ (used by the relay and native client) and the TypeScript moqtail package at ts/moqtail/ (used by the browser client and Meet app). The Rust crate currently identifies as Draft 18-compliant; the repository README describes main as work in progress during the Draft 22 upgrade, with conformance data under dev/conformance/draft22/. When documenting protocol concepts, link both implementations where relevant rather than treating one as canonical.

Versioning uses changesets (.changeset directory) with linked packages, publishing libraries to npm and crates.io. The relay server is published as a container image to ghcr.io/moqtail/relay via the relay.yml workflow. CI is GitHub Actions with separate workflows for Rust (rust.yml), JS (js.yml), misc checks (misc.yml), player checks (player.yml), relay checks (relay.yml), release to npm/crates.io (release-rust.yml, release.yml), and container image building (relay.yml).

pages.title: MOQtail Overview
pages.purpose: High-level introduction to the MOQtail project: what Media-over-QUIC (MOQ) is, why MOQtail exists, the components it ships (Rust and TypeScript libraries, relay, client apps), and how they fit together as an MOQT toolkit during the Draft 22 upgrade.

page_notes.content: Source primarily from the root README.md, which summarizes the TypeScript and Rust libraries, Relay, Getting Started prerequisites/installation, and the academic citation block. Mention the live demo at player.moqtail.dev and the project topics (streaming, real-time, media, MOQ).

pages.title: Repository Structure
pages.purpose: Explain the monorepo organization: the Cargo workspace under rs/, the npm workspace under ts/, the dev/ conformance data, and how Rust and TypeScript components relate to and depend on each other.

page_notes.content: Document the dual workspace setup: root Cargo.toml includes Rust crates via rs/* (rs/moqtail, rs/moqtail-ssts, rs/client, rs/relay). Root package.json defines npm workspaces via ts/* (ts/moqtail, ts/client-js, ts/meet). The dev/conformance/draft22/ directory contains protocol conformance data; scripts/ contains project automation. Note .vscode, .editorconfig, .prettierrc, rustfmt.toml, commitlint.config.ts, and lint-staged.config.js as shared tooling configuration. Root package.json orchestrates npm scripts across workspaces.

pages.title: MOQ Protocol Basics
pages.purpose: Overview of the Media-over-QUIC (MOQT) protocol as defined by IETF draft-ietf-moq-transport, including the Draft 18 implementation and the repository's in-progress Draft 22 upgrade, and the core data model concepts: tracks, namespaces, groups, objects, subscriptions, and fetch.

page_notes.content: Frame this as protocol/domain documentation rather than implementation documentation — it should explain MOQT concepts (control vs data streams, tracks/groups/objects, publisher/subscriber/relay roles, LOC and CMSF media formats mentioned in the repo description) independent of language, then point readers to the Rust and TypeScript library pages for implementation specifics. Cite the IETF draft-ietf-moq-transport spec for protocol terminology.

pages.title: Protocol Libraries
pages.purpose: Section landing page documenting the core protocol implementation libraries shared across the codebase, in both Rust and TypeScript.

page_notes.content: Acts as a parent/index page linking to the Rust moqtail crate, Control Stream Handler, Data Stream Handler, the TypeScript moqtail package, Client API, and Playout Buffer child pages.

pages.title: moqtail (Rust Library)
pages.purpose: Detailed documentation of the Rust protocol library at rs/moqtail/: crate architecture, module layout, key dependencies (e.g. QUIC/WebTransport crates, serde-style serialization), and the public API surface consumed by the relay and native client.

page_notes.content: Start from rs/moqtail/README.md. The crate exposes client, model, relay, and transport modules; model contains catalog, common, control, data, error, parameter, and property modules. Transport handlers are implemented in rs/moqtail/src/transport/control_stream_handler.rs and rs/moqtail/src/transport/data_stream_handler.rs. Cross-link to the Control Stream Handler and Data Stream Handler pages.

pages.title: Control Stream Handler
pages.purpose: Documentation of control message exchange in the Rust moqtail crate: serialization/deserialization of MOQT control messages (SETUP, ANNOUNCE, SUBSCRIBE, FETCH, etc.), timeout handling, and the control-plane communication layer used by both relay and client.

page_notes.content: Located at rs/moqtail/src/transport/control_stream_handler.rs. Document the message enum/struct types, the read/write loop, and how timeouts and malformed-message errors are surfaced to callers (relay Session Management and Message Handlers pages depend on this).

pages.title: Data Stream Handler
pages.purpose: Documentation of data stream transmission and reception in the Rust moqtail crate, including stream abstractions used for object delivery over QUIC/WebTransport streams.

page_notes.content: Document SendDataStream / RecvDataStream APIs, group/object framing on the wire, and how these are consumed by the relay's Track and Subscription system as well as client publisher/subscriber/fetcher modes.

pages.title: moqtail (TypeScript Library)
pages.purpose: Detailed documentation of the TypeScript client library: package structure, build system (bundler/tsconfig), browser/WebTransport integration, and how it's consumed by client-js and the meet app.

page_notes.content: Start from ts/moqtail/README.md. Document the npm package name and exports, build tooling, and browser compatibility (WebTransport requirement); verify usage examples against the current README and source.

pages.title: Client API
pages.purpose: Documentation of the public client API in the TypeScript moqtail package: connection setup, subscribe/fetch operations, publication and namespace management, and request/response handling.

page_notes.content: Verify public API examples and exact method signatures against ts/moqtail/src, and document error handling and the relationship to the Playout Buffer for incoming subscriptions.

pages.title: Playout Buffer
pages.purpose: Documentation of the client-side buffering and timing system that smooths out network jitter for consistent media playback, including latency/target-buffer configuration.

page_notes.content: The main playout buffer implementation lives at ts/meet/src/lib/playout_buffer.ts (used by the Meet app), with a buffer at ts/client-js/src/lib/buffer.ts (used by the browser client). Document configurable latency targets, how it interacts with the Client API's subscribe path, and how it hands frames off to the media pipeline (WebCodecs decoding).

pages.title: Relay Server
pages.purpose: Comprehensive documentation of the relay server architecture — the most critical component, responsible for forwarding MOQT control and data messages between publishers and subscribers. Includes how to run it locally and as a container.

page_notes.content: The relay crate and implementation live under rs/relay/ (rs/relay/src/ and rs/relay/src/server/). Use rs/relay/cert/cert.pem and rs/relay/cert/key.pem for local certificate paths; the certificate generation/browser trust setup is documented in rs/relay/cert/README.md. The Dockerfile is rs/relay/Dockerfile. Docker images are published to ghcr.io/moqtail/relay by .github/workflows/relay.yml; verify current run commands and image tags against the workflow and relay source before documenting them.

pages.title: Server Architecture
pages.purpose: Overview of the relay server's internal architecture: the Server/Session model, how incoming WebTransport/QUIC connections are accepted, and the concurrent (async) processing pattern used per session.

page_notes.content: The entry point is rs/relay/src/main.rs and the server implementation is under rs/relay/src/server/. Document how it binds the QUIC/WebTransport listener and spawns per-session work. Cross-link to Session Management for per-connection detail and Client Management for the registry that spans sessions.

pages.title: Session Management
pages.purpose: Documentation of session lifecycle: connection establishment/teardown, SessionContext state, and control-stream message processing loop for a single client connection.

page_notes.content: Document SessionContext fields (client identity, negotiated parameters, associated streams), the control-stream read loop (built on the Rust moqtail crate's Control Stream Handler), and graceful/error teardown paths. Note interactions with ClientManager for registering/deregistering sessions.

pages.title: Client Management
pages.purpose: Documentation of the MOQTClient abstraction in the relay, partitioned stream management for scaling outbound delivery, message queuing, and the ClientManager registry that tracks all connected clients.

page_notes.content: Document how MOQTClient wraps a session's outbound data streams (partitioned, likely sharded by track or group for parallelism), the queuing/backpressure strategy, and how ClientManager is looked up by Track/Subscription processing when fanning out objects to subscribers.

pages.title: Track and Subscription System
pages.purpose: Section landing page explaining how tracks manage content distribution from publishers and how subscriptions handle per-client delivery, caching, and filtering.

page_notes.content: Index/parent page linking Track Management, Subscription Processing, Caching System, and Message Handlers — together these form the relay's data-plane logic.

pages.title: Track Management
pages.purpose: Documentation of the Track abstraction: subscriber registration/removal, event distribution via partitioned channels, and object logging for replay/caching.

page_notes.content: Document the Track struct's subscriber list, the partitioned broadcast-channel mechanism used to fan out newly published objects without a single bottleneck, and how published objects are logged/handed to the Caching System for fetch support.

pages.title: Subscription Processing
pages.purpose: Documentation of subscription lifecycle (Subscribe -> active -> Unsubscribe/error), filtering of objects by group/object location ranges, per-subscription stream management, and the subscription state machine.

page_notes.content: Document the state machine driving a subscription (pending/active/ended), how SUBSCRIBE filter parameters (e.g. start/end group-object location) are applied to incoming objects, and how a subscription's data stream is opened/closed against the Data Stream Handler from the Rust moqtail crate.

pages.title: Caching System
pages.purpose: Documentation of the TrackCache, built on the moka caching library: eviction policies (TTL/TTI), object storage organized by group, and how the cache backs Fetch (on-demand) requests.

page_notes.content: Document TrackCache's use of moka for TTL/TTI-based eviction, the per-group object storage layout, and how a FETCH control message is resolved against cached objects versus live data. Cross-link to Configuration and Deployment for cache size/TTL configuration knobs.

pages.title: Message Handlers
pages.purpose: Documentation of control message processing in the relay: SUBSCRIBE, FETCH, ANNOUNCE, and UNSUBSCRIBE handlers, and the relay (forwarding) logic that ties publishers to subscribers.

page_notes.content: Document each handler's responsibilities: ANNOUNCE registers a namespace/track with the relay; SUBSCRIBE creates a Subscription against an existing or to-be-announced Track; FETCH resolves against the Caching System; UNSUBSCRIBE/UNANNOUNCE tear down state. Note how handlers depend on ClientManager, Track Management, and Subscription Processing.

pages.title: Configuration and Deployment
pages.purpose: Documentation of relay server configuration: command-line options (port, cert-file, key-file), cache settings, network parameters, TLS certificate setup, and container deployment.

page_notes.content: Document the relay configuration by inspecting rs/relay/src (including server configuration and CLI setup), and link to rs/relay/cert/README.md for local certificate generation and browser trust. Check .github/workflows/relay.yml for current image publishing and tagging behavior.

pages.title: Client Applications
pages.purpose: Section landing page for the client applications that act as publishers or subscribers against the relay: the browser client, the native Rust client, and the Meet video-conferencing demo.

page_notes.content: Index/parent page linking Browser Client (client-js), Native Client (client), and Meet App.

pages.title: Browser Client (client-js)
pages.purpose: Documentation of the Preact-based browser client: UI components, the media pipeline, video decoding, and WebTransport integration with the relay.

page_notes.content: Located at ts/client-js/. Document the UI component tree (including Header, Sidebar, and VideoPlayer), how the ts/moqtail Client API and buffer are wired into the UI, and the video decode path (WebCodecs).

pages.title: Native Client (client)
pages.purpose: Documentation of the Rust-based native client supporting publisher, subscriber, and fetcher modes via a command-line interface, built on the Rust moqtail crate.

page_notes.content: The Rust client is at rs/client/. Document its CLI argument surface and how each mode uses the Rust moqtail crate's control and data stream handlers.

pages.title: Meet App (Video Conferencing Demo)
pages.purpose: Documentation of the React-based video conferencing demo: the media pipeline, WebCodecs-based encoding/decoding, signalling carried over MOQ tracks, and Playout Buffer integration for synchronized playback.

page_notes.content: Located at ts/meet/. Document how signalling (room membership, track announcements) is carried over MOQ tracks, how WebCodecs is used for encoding and decoding, and how it differs from ts/client-js.

pages.title: Development Guide
pages.purpose: Comprehensive guide for developers contributing to MOQtail: environment setup, prerequisites, and day-to-day workflows across the Rust and TypeScript workspaces.

page_notes.content: Base prerequisites per README: Rust toolchain, Node.js 22+, npm, and Docker (for relay container builds/runs). Setup: `git clone https://github.com/moqtail/moqtail.git && cd moqtail && npm install`. Commit requirements (enforced by Husky hooks and CI): every commit must include a `Signed-off-by` line (DCO — Developer Certificate of Origin, appended via `git commit -s`); commit messages must follow Conventional Commits format; user-facing changes require a changeset (prompted by pre-commit hook). A CLA may be requested for significant contributions. Full details in CONTRIBUTING.md.

pages.title: Build System
pages.purpose: Documentation of the build process: the Cargo workspace (Rust crates), npm workspaces (TypeScript packages/apps), and how cross-language dependencies (e.g. shared protocol constants or generated types) are kept consistent.

page_notes.content: The root Cargo.toml includes rs/*; current crates are rs/moqtail, rs/moqtail-ssts, rs/client, and rs/relay. Root package.json defines npm workspaces with ts/*: ts/moqtail, ts/client-js, and ts/meet. Root npm scripts orchestrate TypeScript builds and tests; the package-specific scripts are defined in each workspace. Project scripts live under scripts/ (including postversion.mjs, precommit.mjs, test-client.sh, conformance-test.sh, and perf-test.sh). Conformance data is under dev/conformance/draft22/.

pages.title: Testing Strategy
pages.purpose: Documentation of the testing infrastructure: vitest for TypeScript packages, Rust unit/integration tests via cargo test, and any cross-language or end-to-end integration testing approach.

page_notes.content: Document npm test scripts and Vitest configuration in ts/moqtail/, plus `cargo test` usage for crates under rs/. Cross-reference .github/workflows/rust.yml and .github/workflows/js.yml (badged in the README as 'Rust Checks' and 'JavaScript Checks') for CI behavior, including any relay/client interoperability testing.

pages.title: CI/CD Pipeline
pages.purpose: Documentation of GitHub Actions workflows: pull request checks (Rust and JavaScript), release automation (changesets-driven publishing), container image builds/pushes to GHCR, and documentation deployment.

page_notes.content: Workflows under .github/workflows/ currently include rust.yml, js.yml, misc.yml, player.yml, meet.yml, relay.yml, release-rust.yml, and release.yml. Document checks and release behavior by consulting the relevant workflow files; relay images are published to ghcr.io/moqtail/relay.

pages.title: Versioning and Releases
pages.purpose: Documentation of the changesets-based release workflow: semantic versioning, linked/grouped packages, and publishing to npm (TypeScript) and crates.io (Rust), plus relay container image releases.

page_notes.content: Document the changeset authoring flow (adding a changeset per PR), how linked packages are configured (for example, the TypeScript moqtail package and its dependents), and the release tag convention `relay@x.y.z` used to trigger relay image publishing.

pages.title: Code Quality Tools
pages.purpose: Documentation of linting, formatting, commit message conventions, and pre-commit hooks enforced across the project.

page_notes.content: Document Prettier configuration (including per-app .prettierrc files) and rustfmt.toml as the formatters for TypeScript and Rust, .editorconfig for cross-editor consistency, commitlint.config.ts for commit message format, lint-staged.config.js for staged-file checks, and .husky/ hooks that wire these tools into contributor workflows.
